page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfr6.8xlarge is a memory-optimized server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated physical cores on an x86_64 architecture, utilizing the Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at a clock speed of 3.1 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 256.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. The processor is equipped with 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 35 MB of L3 cache. It supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX, AVX-512, and AES cryptography. This instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage and featuring a baseline network bandwidth of 10 Gbps.

In benchmark evaluations, the ecs.hfr6.8xlarge demonstrates stable mid-range performance. The Intel Xeon processor achieves a single-core stress-ng score of 1436.69 and a multi-core score of 30656.07, while the Passmark CPU score reaches 29575.82. Memory performance is highlighted by a read-only small block cached bandwidth of 1704.61 GB/sec, which drops to 112.52 GB/sec for large uncached blocks, alongside a write bandwidth of 49.63 GB/sec. The instance handles database operations efficiently, registering 11530.5 on the Passmark database test and processing 28.86 million operations per second in Redis SET workloads. For specialized tasks, it records a Geekbench multi-core score of 11147.0 and a software compilation score of 23685.0.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.hfr6.8xlarge offers a high-density memory profile relative to its compute resources, making it a viable option for memory-intensive workloads that do not require local NVMe storage or GPU acceleration. The absence of bundled local storage means storage costs are decoupled, allowing for flexible network storage scaling. This instance is well-suited for high-performance databases, in-memory caching layers like Redis, enterprise applications, and moderate data processing tasks. It can also support lightweight machine learning inference, as demonstrated by its ability to process 46.27 tokens per second on a 7B parameter model.
